questions.question: What is the primary difference between a scalar and a vector?

Time

questions.question: What is the primary goal of the gradient descent algorithm in machine learning?
options: To find the minimum of a cost or loss function
To maximize the amount of data processed
To increase the learning rate over time
To calculate the maximum error possible

questions.question: What does a 'loss function' or 'cost function' represent in machine learning?
options: The total number of parameters
The amount of data lost during processing
The error or difference between predicted and actual values
The speed of the algorithm

questions.question: In mathematics, the gradient of a function points in which direction?
options: The direction of the absolute minimum
The direction of a slope of zero
The direction of the steepest ascent (greatest increase) of the function
The direction of the y-axis only

questions.question: Why does gradient descent subtract the gradient from the current weights?
options: Because moving against the gradient ensures we step towards the local minimum
Because weights must always be negative numbers
Because addition is computationally too slow

questions.question: What role does the 'learning rate' play in gradient descent?

questions.question: What happens if the learning rate in gradient descent is set too low?
options: The algorithm will bounce wildly around the minimum
The algorithm will run backwards
The algorithm will take an extremely long time to converge to the minimum

options: The absolute lowest point on the entire loss curve
A low point on the curve that is not the lowest possible overall point
The point where the loss is completely zero

questions.question: What is the 'global minimum' in a loss function?
